JISHUMI:v1p892/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p892/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p892/r5.claim: Iʿtizal means withdrawing or moving away; Jishumi compares the usage in the Cave youths' story and Abraham's withdrawal.
JISHUMI:v1p892/r5.anchor: والاعتزال: التنحي عن الشيء، وكل شيء نحيته فقد عزلته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r11.claim: In “I call upon my Lord,” the author understands calling as worship, in keeping with the parallel phrase “I worship my Lord.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p271/r11.anchor: والأظهر أن قوله وأدعوا ربي معناه وأعبد ربي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r1.speaker: الحديث
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r1.claim: A hadith says that supplication is worship.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r2.claim: The supplication may be the prayer Abraham recited in al-Shuʿaraʾ, asking for wisdom and joining the righteous.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد الدعاء الذي حكاه الله في سورة الشعراء رب هب لي حكما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r3.claim: Abraham contrasts the unbelievers' invocation of their gods with his humble hope in his Lord; the word ʿasā combines hope with intense fear and self-effacement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r3.anchor: عسى ألا أكون بدعاء ربي شقيا مع التواضع لله في كلمة عسى

BURSEVI:v5p259#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p259#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p259#2/r1.claim: Abraham will emigrate away from his family and their idols because his advice failed, worship God alone, and humbly hopes not to be disappointed in prayer.
BURSEVI:v5p259#2/r1.anchor: أتباعد عنك وعن قومك بالمهاجرة بديني حيث لم يؤثر فيكم نصائحي

BURSEVI:v5p259#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p259#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p259#2/r2.claim: Beginning with perhaps shows humility and good manners.
BURSEVI:v5p259#2/r2.anchor: وفي تصدير الكلام بعسى إظهار التواضع ومراعاة حسن الأدب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r1.claim: “I will leave you” apparently coordinates with “I will seek forgiveness”: Abraham will separate from his father and people by migrating because his counsel had no effect.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r2.claim: Reports say Abraham migrated to Syria, or to nearby Harran, while his people were in Kutha.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r2.anchor: وقيل إلى حران وهو قريب من ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r3.claim: A spiritual interpretation takes the separation as inward separation in heart and belief, but al-Alusi calls this contrary to the apparent and transmitted sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r3.anchor: وجوز حمل على العتزال بالقلب والاعتقاد وهو خلاف الظاهر المأثور

ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r4.claim: Calling on God means worshipping Him alone; “worship” answers the father's complaint about abandoning idols, while “call” more clearly expresses the positive turn toward God.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r4.anchor: أي اعبده سبحانه وحده كما يفهم من اجتناب غيره تعالى من المعبودات

ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r5.claim: The call may mean supplication generally, or Abraham's prayers for wisdom and the company of the righteous, or for a righteous child.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r5.anchor: وجوز أن يراد بذلك الدعاء مطلق

ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r6.claim: “Wretched” means disappointed and unsuccessful; the wording indirectly contrasts Abraham's hope with his people's misery in worshipping idols.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r6.anchor: خائبا ضائع السعى وفيه تعريض بشقاوتهم في عبادة الهتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r7.claim: Beginning with “perhaps” shows humility and proper etiquette, since acceptance is God's favor rather than an obligation and the final outcome is among the unseen matters known to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#2/r7.anchor: وفي تصدير الكلام بعسى من اظهار التواضع ومراعاة حسن الأدب والتنبيه على حقيقة الحق من أن الاثابه والأجابة بطريق التفضل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r9.speaker: أبو تراب النخشبي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r9.claim: Abu Turab al-Nakhshabi says keeping company with wicked people breeds suspicion of the good; scripture and experience show it hardens the heart and discourages good.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r9.anchor: وعن أبى تراب النخشبى صحبة الأشرار تورث سوء الظن بالاخيار

ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r10.claim: Abraham's prayer displays exceptional courtesy toward God, as the station of intimate friendship requires; one without proper courtesy cannot be God's friend.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r10.anchor: فيه من الدلالة على مزيد ادبه عليه السلام مع ربه عز وجل ما فيه ومقام الخلة يقتضى ذلك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r9.claim: Abraham's separation from his people includes separation from what they worship besides God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r9.anchor: {وأعتزلكم وما تدعون من دون الله} أي: أعتزل ما تعبدون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r10.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r10.claim: Muqatil says Abraham left his people at Kutha and emigrated to the Holy Land.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r10.anchor: مقاتل: كان اعتزاله إياهم أنه فارقهم من "كوثى"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r11.claim: Calling on Abraham's Lord means worshipping Him and hoping not to be wretched as the idolaters are through their worship.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r11.anchor: {وأدعو ربي} أي: أعبد ربي {عسى ألا أكون بدعاء ربي شقيا}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r12.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r12.claim: Another interpretation hopes God will answer Abraham when called and not disappoint him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r12.anchor: وقيل: عسى أن يجيبني إذا دعوته ولا يخيبني.

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:48-49/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:48-49/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:48-49/r1.claim: Abraham migrates for his faith and worships God alone; “perhaps” expresses humility, recognizes that prayer and reward are gifts rather than obligations, and acknowledges the unseen outcome.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:48-49/r1.anchor: { وأعتزلكم وما تدعون من دون الله } بالمهاجرة بديني

BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r4.claim: Abraham will leave his people and their deities for as long as they persist in their religion, and worship his Lord alone as the one worthy of invocation in hardship.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r4.anchor: وما تدعون } أي تعبدون { من دون الله

BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r5.claim: His “perhaps” humbly leaves acceptance to God and allows for the trials of worldly life; he hopes not to be wretched in prayer as idolaters are, since idols neither answer nor harm.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r5.anchor: فقال غير جازم بإجابة دعوته وقبول عبادته

BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r6.speaker: أبو سليمان الخطابي
BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r6.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī says a person's deepest estrangement is lack of like-minded companions, not distance from home.

QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r9.claim: Abraham's devotion was wholly sincere: neither blame nor temptation to favor himself turned him from God.
QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r9.anchor: مخلصا خالصا لله ، ولم يكن لغيره بوجه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r11.claim: Tadʿūn means “you worship”; Abraham will move apart from his people and their idols.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r11.anchor: وتدعون بمعنى تعبدون، وقوله عسى، ترج، في ضمنه خوف شديد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r12.claim: The word ʿasā expresses hope while containing deep apprehension.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r12.anchor: وقوله عسى، ترج، في ضمنه خوف شديد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p238/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p238/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p238/r1.claim: Abraham will withdraw from his people and from their idols.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p238/r1.anchor: وأعتزلكم أي وأتنحى عنكم وأعتزل ما تدعون من دون الله يعني الأصنام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p238/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p238/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p238/r2.claim: Tadʿūna may mean that they worship the idols or that they call them gods.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p238/r2.anchor: وفي معنى تدعون قولان أحدهما تعبدون والثاني أن المعنى وما تدعونه ربا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p238/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p238/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p238/r3.claim: Abraham hopes not to be disappointed in worshiping God as his people were in worshiping idols, which neither help nor answer prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p238/r3.anchor: أرجو أن لا أشقى بعبادته كما شقيتم أنتم بعبادة الأصنام لأنها لا تنفعهم

SULAMI:v1p427#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p427#4/r1.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v1p427#4/r1.claim: To secure outward and inward safety in this world and the next, one should leave bad companions and seek God's help to part from them; a person follows those he loves, as a companion follows his companion.
SULAMI:v1p427#4/r1.anchor: قال القاسم : من أراد السلامة في الدنيا والآخرة ظاهرا وباطنا فليعتزل قرناء السوء

SULAMI:v1p427#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p427#4/r2.speaker: أبو تراب النخشبي
SULAMI:v1p427#4/r2.claim: Keeping bad company breeds suspicion of good people.
SULAMI:v1p427#4/r2.anchor: وقال أبو تراب النخشبي : صحبة الأشرار تورث ( سوء الظن ) بالأخيار

SULAMI:v1p427#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p427#4/r3.speaker: عبد العزيز المكي
SULAMI:v1p427#4/r3.claim: Abraham approached prayer with shame and awe, fearing his tongue might be unworthy of remembering God; he hoped God would excuse his unfitness and not make him wretched for calling upon Him.
SULAMI:v1p427#4/r3.anchor: قال عبد العزيز المكي : كان الخليل عليه السلام يهاب ربه أن يدعوه ، ويذكره ، ويعظمه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p236/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p236/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p236/r1.claim: Abraham separates from his people, disavows their idols, and worships God alone without partner.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p236/r1.anchor: أي: أجتنبكم وأتبرأ منكم ومن آلهتكم التي تعبدونها [من دون الله] (6)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p236/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p236/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p236/r2.claim: Abraham's hope not to be wretched in supplication is certain to be fulfilled, since he is the greatest prophet after Muhammad.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p236/r2.anchor: و "عسى" هذه موجبة لا محالة، فإنه عليه السلام، سيد الأنبياء بعد محمد

JISHUMI:v6p4571/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r1.claim: Abraham chooses religion over helping his father and emigration over homeland; he withdraws from them and their worship.
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r1.anchor: ثم بين أنه يختار الدين على مساعدة الأب، والهجرة على الوطن

JISHUMI:v6p4571/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r2.speaker: غير مسمى
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r2.claim: What they call upon means idols; alternatively, calling means worship.

JISHUMI:v6p4571/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r3.claim: Here ʿasā expresses certainty: Abraham will not be wretched in praying to his Lord as his people were in praying to idols; he speaks humbly.
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r3.anchor: عسى هو هنا واجب ومعناه: لا أكون بدعاء ربي شقيا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r9.claim: Abraham's separation means migration to Syria; duʿāʾ here means worship, since prayer is part and one of worship's means, as 19:49 confirms.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r10.speaker: الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r10.claim: The Prophet says that supplication is worship.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r10.anchor: قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 664 ) ( الدعاء هو العبادة )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r11.claim: Alternatively, duʿāʾ means the supplication recorded in 26:83–89; Abraham hints that his family is wretched in invoking idols, while his own hope is expressed humbly with ʿasā.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p23/r11.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد الدعاء الذي حكاه الله

FARRA:v2p169/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p169/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p169/r4.claim: Abraham means that if he calls upon his Lord, he will not be made miserable by the prayer.
FARRA:v2p169/r4.anchor: وقوله: عسى ألا أكون بدعاء ربي شقيا [48] يقول: إن دعوته لم أشق به.

MUQATIL:19:45-48/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:45-48/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:45-48/r6.claim: Ibrahim separates from his family and their idols, leaving Kutha for the Holy Land; he will pray for his father's forgiveness, hoping not to be disappointed.
MUQATIL:19:45-48/r6.anchor: فكان اعتزاله إياهم أنه فارقهم من كوثا، فهاجر منها إلى الأرض المقدسة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#3/r1.claim: Abraham's separation means migration from Babylon to Syria; what his people invoke besides God means their idols.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#3/r1.anchor: أراد بالاعتزال المهاجرة من أرض بابل إلى الشام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#3/r2.claim: دعوا means worship, and Abraham's expression of hope humbles himself while hinting at his people's wretchedness for worshipping idols.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#3/r2.anchor: واعبد ﴿ ربي ﴾ ثم قال تواضعا وهضما للنفس ومعرضا بشقاوتهم بدعاء آلهتهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#3/r3.claim: He hopes not to fail by worshipping his Lord as they failed through worshipping idols.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#3/r3.anchor: أي كما شقيتم أنتم بعبادة الأصنام

MAJAZ:v2p6/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p6/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p6/r4.claim: كان الله عليما حكيما can span the past, present, and future; كان may also be extra and have no syntactic effect, as the cited lines and Qays ibn Ghālib’s report illustrate.
MAJAZ:v2p6/r4.anchor: «وكان الله عليما حكيما» (48/ 4) فيما مضى والساعة، وفيما يكون ويجيء «كان» أيضا زائدة ولا تعمل فى الاسم

MAJAZ:v2p6/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p6/r5.speaker: قيس بن غالب
MAJAZ:v2p6/r5.claim: Qays ibn Ghālib al-Badrī says Fāṭima bint al-Kharshab’s sons were so exceptional that no كان مثلهم means no people like them were found; كان is extra.
MAJAZ:v2p6/r5.anchor: وسمعت قيس بن غالب البدرى يقول: ولدت فاطمة بنت الخرشب الكملة من بنى عبس لم يوجد كان مثلهم

QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r12.claim: Iʿtizal means separation; its fuller discussion occurred earlier in al-Kahf.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r12.anchor: العزلة المفارقة وقد تقدم في «الكهف» بيانها.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r13.claim: The most apparent interpretation is that Abraham hoped prayer would bring family and children to ease his loneliness after separating from his people.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r13.anchor: قيل: أراد بهذا الدعاء أن يهب الله تعالى له أهلا وولدا يتقوى بهم حتى لا يستوحش بالاعتزال عن قومه.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r14.claim: Another view says asa teaches that a servant cannot be certain he will remain upon knowledge in the future.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r14.anchor: وقيل: «عسى» يدل على أن العبد لا يقطع بأنه يبقى على المعرفة أم لا في المستقبل.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r15.claim: Another view says Abraham prayed for his father's guidance; asa marks uncertainty about whether the prayer would be answered, though the preceding interpretation is preferred.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r15.anchor: وقيل: دعا لأبيه بالهداية. ف«عسى» شك لأنه كان لا يدري هل يستجاب له فيه أم لا؟ والأول أظهر.

RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r15.claim: Abraham will separate both geographically and religiously from his people and their idols, worshipping the Lord who creates and benefits rather than harmful idols.
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r15.anchor: أفارقكم في المكان وأفارقكم في طريقتكم أيضا وأبعد عنكم وأتشاغل بعبادة ربي الذي ينفع ويضر

RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r16.claim: “I hope not to be wretched in calling my Lord” expresses humility, as does Abraham’s “I hope” in al-Shu‘ara.
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r16.anchor: أرجو أن لا أكون كذلك ، وإنما ذكر ذلك على سبيل التواضع كقوله : { والذى أطمع أن يغفر لى خطيئتى

RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r17.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r17.claim: Calling on his Lord also insinuates that his people are wretched for calling on idols, which cannot hear or benefit anyone.
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r17.anchor: تعريض بشقاوتهم في دعاء آلهتهم على ما قرره أولا في / قوله : { لم * تعبد ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر

STUDYQURAN:19:48/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:48/r1.speaker: Ṭabarī
STUDYQURAN:19:48/r1.claim: Abraham promises to leave his family and their idols, understood by some as departing for the Holy Land.
STUDYQURAN:19:48/r1.anchor: This is understood as his taking leave of his family to migrate to the Holy Land

STUDYQURAN:19:48/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:48/r2.speaker: Ṭabarī
STUDYQURAN:19:48/r2.claim: Although shaqiyyan can mean one who suffers perdition in the Hereafter, here it more likely means that God will answer Abraham's supplications, as in Zachariah's similar statement.
STUDYQURAN:19:48/r2.anchor: more likely means that God will answer his prayers and supplications

STUDYQURAN:19:48/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:48/r3.speaker: Quran commentators
STUDYQURAN:19:48/r3.claim: Abraham's prayer likely asks for family and children to strengthen him after separation; Isaac and Jacob are the answer, fitting the sūrah's theme of blessed children as divine compassion.
STUDYQURAN:19:48/r3.anchor: Abraham is said to have called upon his Lord to grant him family and children

STUDYQURAN:19:48/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:48/r4.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:19:48/r4.claim: An alternative says Abraham prayed for his father's guidance, but the author finds this less likely because the Quran says that guidance did not occur.
STUDYQURAN:19:48/r4.anchor: this seems less likely, since according to the Quran this guidance does not come to pass

NAHHAS:v3p18/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p18/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p18/r7.claim: ما is accusative by coordination, meaning Abraham would leave what his people invoked besides God.
NAHHAS:v3p18/r7.anchor: ما في موضع نصب لأنها معطوفة أي واعتزل ما تدعون

TAB-FULL:v15p556/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p556/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p556/r1.claim: Abraham tells his father “peace upon you,” meaning he will not retaliate or return to the matter his father disliked after the threat.
TAB-FULL:v15p556/r1.anchor: يا أبت، يقول: أمنة مني لك أن أعاودك فيما كرهت،

TAB-FULL:v15p556/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p556/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p556/r2.claim: He will not resume what his father disliked, but will ask God to forgive him by concealing his sins and sparing their punishment.
TAB-FULL:v15p556/r2.anchor: يقول: أمنة مني لك أن أعاودك فيما كرهت، ولدعائك إلي ما توعدتني عليه بالعقوبة ولكني {سأستغفر لك ربي}

TABATABAI:19:47-50/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:47-50/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:47-50/r5.claim: Abraham promises to leave his people and their idols to devote his supplication to God; he speaks hopefully because prayer does not obligate God to reward, and outcomes remain unknown.
TABATABAI:19:47-50/r5.anchor: وعد باعتزالهم والإبتعاد منهم ومن أصنامهم ليخلو بربه ويخلص الدعاء له رجاء

TABATABAI:19:47-50/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:47-50/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:47-50/r6.claim: The request not to be wretched expresses the believer’s proper movement between fear and hope, since divine reward is freely bestowed and final outcomes are unseen.
TABATABAI:19:47-50/r6.anchor: فعلى المؤمن أن يسير بين الخوف والرجاء

TABRISI:19:45-48/r23.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:45-48/r23.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:45-48/r23.claim: Ibrahim withdraws from his people and their idols, worships his Lord, and hopes not to be frustrated as they are by invoking idols.
TABRISI:19:45-48/r23.anchor: وأتنحى منكم جانبا وأعتزل عبادة ما تدعون من دونه من الأصنام

TABRISI:19:45-48/r24.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:45-48/r24.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:45-48/r24.claim: Ibrahim says ʿasā as an expression of humility before God.
TABRISI:19:45-48/r24.anchor: وإنما ذكر عسى على وجه الخضوع

TABRISI:19:49-50/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:49-50/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:49-50/r1.claim: Ibrahim hopes God will accept his worship rather than reject him; a believer combines hope with fear.
TABRISI:19:49-50/r1.anchor: وقيل: معناه لعله يقبل طاعتي وعبادتي ولا أشقى بالرد فإن المؤمن بين الرجاء والخوف

THALABI:v6p217/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p217/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p217/r6.claim: Abraham’s resolve is to leave his people and the idols they worship.
THALABI:v6p217/r6.anchor: وأعتزلكم وما تدعون من دون الله يعني وأعتزل ما تعبدون من دون الله

THALABI:v6p217/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p217/r7.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v6p217/r7.claim: Muqatil says Abraham left his people at Kutha and migrated to the Holy Land.
THALABI:v6p217/r7.anchor:
قال مقاتل:
كان اعتزاله إياهم أنه فارقهم من كوثى فهاجر منها إلى الأرض المقدسة

THALABI:v6p217/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p217/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p217/r8.claim: Abraham hopes his prayer will be answered and he will not be disappointed; alternatively, he hopes not to suffer through worship as idolaters do.
THALABI:v6p217/r8.anchor:
عسى أن يجيبني ولا يخيبني، وقيل:
معناه عسى أن لا أشقى بدعائه وعبادته كما تشقون أنتم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p259/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p259/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p259/r4.claim: Abraham will withdraw from his people and from the idols they worship, worshipping his Lord and hoping not to be wretched by prayer; this implies their idols bring misery because they neither help nor answer prayer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p259/r4.anchor: قوله تعالى: {وأعتزلكم} أي: أتنحى عنكم وأفارقكم.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:47-50/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:47-50/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:47-50/r4.claim: Abraham leaves his people and their idols to worship God, hoping not to be miserable as they were; he means God will accept and reward his worship.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:47-50/r4.anchor: وأعتزلكم وما تدعون } أفارقكم وأفارق ما تعبدون من أصنامكم { وأدعو ربي } أعبده { عسى أن لا أكون بدعاء ربي } بعبادته { شقيا } كما شقيتم أنتم بعبادة الأصنام. يريد: إنه يتقبل عبادتي ويثيبني عليها.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r14.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r14.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r14.claim: The objects Abraham and his people worship besides God are their idols.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p228/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p228/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p228/r1.claim: Abraham hopes that praying to his Lord will make him happy rather than wretched.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:42/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:42/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:42/r1.claim: Abraham repeatedly addressed his father Azar respectfully as my father despite his idolatry and threats; the passage shows a younger person may advise an elder and that true religious guidance comes from revelation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:42/r1.anchor: Hz. İbrâhim, babası Âzer’e her sözünün başında “babacığım” diye hitap etmekte

ASAD-NOTES:19:47#n35/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:47#n35/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:19:47#n35/r1.claim: Abraham's phrase literally means that he hopes not to be unfortunate in prayer to his Sustainer.
ASAD-NOTES:19:47#n35/r1.anchor: that I will not be unfortunate in the prayer to my Sustainer

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Abraham's declaration of disavowal shows his lack of concern for public opinion and his trust in God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: lack of concern at what people would say and trust in God is evident from every word of this declaration

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Despite his kindness, Abraham would not compromise through fear or courtesy: he formally disavowed his family and their deities.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: He did not offer any compromise because of his gracious behaviour or because of any fear and expressly declared his acquittal from them and from their deities.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The plural form extends Abraham's disavowal beyond his father to his companions, associates, family, and the deities they invoke; he then affirms worship of God alone.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: not only proclaimed acquittal from his father but also from all his companions, associates and members of the family.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Abraham's closing confidence expresses trust that God will guide and support him; the preacher of truth must combine softness with firmness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: It is in fact this amalgam of soft and stern attitude which distinguishes a preacher of truth from others.
